narrative: Global equity markets rally with DAX, NASDAQ and Asian indices all posting solid overnight gains, supporting a risk-on continuation into Nordic trading. OMX30 sits in confirmed bull regime (+5.2% above 200-MA) with moderate ADX (24.4) and neutral RSI (55.14)—room to run but no extreme momentum. Weakness in EUR/SEK and USD/SEK both favor Swedish large-cap exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson). Gold and copper strength directly support Boliden. However, the 64bp jump in US 10Y yields is a double-edged sword: Banks widen NIM but Tech faces DCF compression; oil weakness (-2.58%) relieves input cost pressure on industrials. Watch for mean reversion risk if RSI approaches 70 or ADX softens below 18.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to strong global risk sentiment—DAX, NASDAQ and Asia all bid overnight. Index remains firmly in bull regime above 200-MA (+5.2%), MACD below signal but ADX 24.4 shows moderate bullish lean; RSI 55 is neutral and offers room to extend. Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance at 3180 (50-MA). Exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) benefit from SEK weakness; Boliden catches bid from gold +1.16% and copper +1.13%. Banks gain from 64bp yield surge but watch Tech for DCF headwinds. Oil at 97.73 (-2.58%) eases input-cost concern for Industrials. Main watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—any surprise could reignite rate volatility. Sector call: Overweight Industrials & Banks, neutral Tech, long Boliden.

topRisk: US yield volatility: 64bp jump in 10Y suggests market pricing in higher-for-longer rates. If claims data disappoints (jobless spike), expect flight-to-safety and potential OMX30 pullback to 3085. Trade tensions or geopolitical headlines could also trigger rapid VIX spike and unwind commodity/exporter strength.
